title: Normative Robustness as a Frontier for Non-Verifiable Reasoning in LLMs

bias_targets.methodology: Measuring 'moral deliberative sycophancy' by explicitly injecting a simulated user's preferred moral view (for or against an action) during multi-turn moral dilemmas, and evaluating whether the LLM shifts its final judgment and rationalizations to align with the user's stated viewpoint.

Measuring models' structural robustness by varying the presentation order of pro and con arguments (e.g., pro-then-con vs. con-then-pro) across single-turn and multi-turn conversations to detect recency and priming effects on the final moral judgment.
